newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge forces fight brief internal battle.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge forces fight brief internal battle.

text.p: Fighting erupted briefly between Khmer Rouge units in their last stronghold on Friday amid reports that hated strongman Pol Pot had killed a rival and fled, Cambodian government officials said.
"This morning from 9 a.m. to 10 a.m., there was fighting between Khmer Rouge rebels...in Anlong Veng," Leng Sochea, director of the government press department, told Reuters.
Senior military adviser Tom Sambol said the fighting was between Khmer Rouge hardliners loyal to Pol Pot and a breakaway group of guerrillas who have defected to the goverment.

Earlier on Friday Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said Pol Pot, mastermind of the 1975-1979 "killing fields" rule, had killed his defence chief and 11 members of his family and fled the northern stronghold with 200 fighters and the Maoist movement's nominal leader as hostage.
He told reporters that Pol Pot had accused his defence chief Son Sen of allying with Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

Ranariddh, speaking at a school opening, said Pol Pot killed Son Sen and his family members by shooting them and running over the bodies with a truck. He then fled with the group's nominal leader, Khieu Samphan, as hostage.
Ranariddh's announcement came after several reports of recent infighting among the remaining hardline rebels, whose brutal rule killed more than one million Cambodians during the 1970s.
Both Ranariddh and Hun Sen have been trying to woo breakaway Khmer Rouge rebels ahead of national elections scheduled for next year.
The Maoist guerrilla movement began unraveling last August when a senior rebel, Ieng Sary, broke with hardliners and eventually forged peace with the government.
Since then, thousands of rebels have defected to government ranks and fewer than 2,000 troops are thought to remain in Anlong Veng.

Tom Sambol and Leng Sochea said a large group of rebels had fled about five km (miles) east of Anlong Veng after Friday's fighting. The fleeing fighters were rebels loyal to Pol Pot, according to Tom Sambol, but Leng Sochea said the troops had not been identified.
There were apparently some casualties, but no figures were available, Tom Sambol said.
General Long Sereyrath said government forces had intercepted radio transmissions around Anlong Veng and that rebels were heard arguing over the radio and abusing each other.

A division about 2,000 government troops, including 600 former Khmer Rouge who defected to the government several months ago, had been dispatched to the area to investigate, according to the Defence Ministry office of general staff.
The Khmer Rouge, who reneged on a 1991 peace pact, has been fighting a low-intensity war against the coalition government formed after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
